What to clarify in the quote

  • Expected monthly copy volume, scan frequency, and number of users.

  • Whether toner, service calls, delivery, and installation are included.
  • How replacement or upgrade requests are handled when teams grow.

Plan monthly copy volume before choosing the unit

  • Separate daily admin copies from billing runs, enrollment periods, clinic records, training modules, or board-report peaks.
  • Estimate monthly pages by department so one heavy Cubao or Eastwood team does not hide behind a low company average.
  • Ask whether the quote changes when volume increases, when duplex is required, or when color output becomes recurring.
  • Use the QC volume planning guide before approving the final model.

Map scan workflow needs early

  • Confirm who needs scan-to-email, scan-to-folder, shared network access, or front-desk scanning.
  • List users by department so permissions and placement can be planned before delivery.
  • Flag clinics, schools, property teams, and back-office groups that scan more often than they copy.
  • Use the QC scan workflow checklist when document routing is the bigger issue.

Confirm delivery and building access

  • State whether the office is in Cubao, Eastwood, Vertis North, Timog, Tomas Morato, Diliman, Commonwealth, or another QC district.
  • Share elevator access, loading area, delivery window, floor level, security registration, and any hallway or reception constraints.
  • Confirm the target setup date and whether work must happen before office hours, after office hours, or during a controlled building window.

Set maintenance expectations before approval

  • Ask how toner, preventive maintenance, emergency service calls, and replacement planning are handled.
  • Clarify response path if a shared copier blocks billing, admissions, clinic records, or property-office paperwork.
  • Check whether the agreement can adjust if user count, copy volume, or scan demand grows after installation.
  • Ask what usage details the team should report when requesting service so troubleshooting is faster.
